title: sprint-04: LangGraph planning assistant over the forecast database
goal: An assistant that answers planning questions from the stored forecasts and their measured errors, and cannot state a number the database does not hold. Read-only typed SQL tools, every tool call logged, conversation state checkpointed to Postgres, preferences remembered across conversations, a killed run resumable.
pattern: LangGraph StateGraph (route, model, tools, answer) + Postgres checkpointer and store + read-only role
findings: Tests: 184 passed in 441.16s (0:07:21) (real Postgres test database, scripted offline model).

Kill-and-resume proof on the real database: 8 of 8 checks passed. child exit code: 137 in the first process; a second process resumed the thread; the tool that had finished was not run again (same finish time, attempts = 1).
Resumed answer, every number taken from a tool result: The forecast high for 2026-11-15 is 72.1 F. Day-ahead published forecasts have missed by 2.2 F on average.

Two defects found by the proof and fixed: the read-only role had no grant on marts built before it existed; checkpoints were written in the background, so a hard kill could race the save (now written synchronously).

Live run against Claude (run/live.out): 5 questions, 9 tool calls. 4 answers passed the number check; 1 was refused because the rewritten answer still held a number that is in no tool result. Preferences saved in one conversation were used in a new one.

Seen in the live run, and not caught: an answer stated a 0.5 F gap that the model had subtracted itself. It passed because 0.5 appears elsewhere in the same tool result. The check matches digits, not meaning.
commands: make agent Q="Is Saturday warm enough for the beach?"

limits: The number check is strict on purpose: a figure the model works out itself (a sum, a difference, a unit conversion) is refused even when it is right.

The number check reads digits. It does not check that a number is attached to the right day or the right quantity, and it does not check words ('warm', 'likely'). A figure the model computes passes if the same digits happen to be in a tool result; the live run shows one such case.
One local user. Threads are not access-controlled: anyone who can reach the site and knows a thread id can read that conversation.
The live run is five questions read by hand, not a scored evaluation. A scored question set against the live model is sprint 05.
The 79 mutants of sprints 01-03 were not rerun this sprint (the machine was short of memory); the mutation figure above covers the sprint-04 files only.
A tool cut off mid-query is run again on resume. That is safe here because every data tool is read-only.
